scenes.tts: Chapter one showed why a membrane protein keeps its direction during traffic. But lipids are not locked in place. How does a cell keep different lipids on the two faces while molecules still move?
scenes.visual: Continue chapter 1's schematic cell and colour map: cytosol soft gold, outside and route lumens teal, membranes grey, carried type I protein blue with yellow N end, green C end and orange sugar. Label 'schematic' in a corner. The chapter 1 protein rides from ER to surface without flipping. Then camera fills the frame with one plasma-membrane patch. The protein remains oriented while large labelled lipid tokens begin gliding laterally in both leaflets. A question mark grows between the visibly different rows.
scenes.narration: Chapter one showed why a membrane protein keeps its direction during traffic. But lipids are not locked in place. How does a cell keep different lipids on the two faces while molecules still move?

scenes.visual: Over the moving membrane patch, show the title 'Across or Along the Membrane?' for two seconds. Lipid tokens continue drifting behind it, then the title dissolves.

scenes.tts: A red blood cell gives the best-measured example. P S and P E sit mainly on the cytoplasmic leaflet. P C and sphingomyelin sit mainly outside. Sideways drifting does not erase that pattern.
scenes.caption: A red blood cell gives the best-measured example. PS and PE sit mainly on the cytoplasmic leaflet. PC and sphingomyelin sit mainly outside. Sideways drifting does not erase that pattern.
scenes.visual: A red blood cell outline expands to fill most of the frame, then its edge straightens into a two-row membrane. Use labelled tokens only, never molecular structures: yellow 'PS' and green 'PE' tokens populate the gold cytoplasmic row; blue 'PC' and red 'sphingomyelin' tokens populate the teal outer row. Keep at most six representative tokens visible. All tokens slide slowly along their own row while the pattern labels remain fixed.
scenes.narration: A red blood cell gives the best-measured example. PS and PE sit mainly on the cytoplasmic leaflet. PC and sphingomyelin sit mainly outside. Sideways drifting does not erase that pattern.

scenes.tts: Crossing is different. A phospholipid's polar head rarely enters the membrane's oily core unaided. Without help, most phospholipids change leaflets slowly. Slow is not zero, so cells spend energy to maintain asymmetry.
scenes.visual: Track one yellow PS token as it glides freely along the lower row. It turns toward the grey membrane core, meets a wide amber barrier labelled 'oily core', and eases back. A faint clock marked 'slow' turns while occasional ghost copies suggest rare crossing. Then an ATP gauge appears beside a gap in the barrier; its needle rises as the unequal rows sharpen.
scenes.narration: Crossing is different. A phospholipid's polar head rarely enters the membrane's oily core unaided. Without help, most phospholipids change leaflets slowly. Slow is not zero, so cells spend energy to maintain asymmetry.

scenes.tts: An A T P driven flippase selects lipids such as P S and P E and moves them inward. A scramblase does something different. When switched on, it lets lipids cross both ways without energy. The two leaflets then mix.
scenes.caption: An ATP-driven flippase selects lipids such as PS and PE and moves them inward. A scramblase does something different. When switched on, it lets lipids cross both ways without energy. The two leaflets then mix.
scenes.visual: Transform the barrier gap into a labelled block 'flippase'. An ATP token enters; one outer PS token passes through a one-way inward gate and joins the gold row. Transform that block into 'scramblase'; remove the ATP token and open a two-way gate. Yellow, green, blue and red tokens cross in both directions until both rows show the same colour mix. Label the final state 'mixed'.
scenes.narration: An ATP-driven flippase selects lipids such as PS and PE and moves them inward. A scramblase does something different. When switched on, it lets lipids cross both ways without energy. The two leaflets then mix.

scenes.tts: Together, slow leakage, pumps, and regulated scrambling create a steady state, not a permanent arrangement. Flippases keep restoring selected lipids. Switching on a scramblase lets the pattern collapse.
scenes.visual: Split the membrane into a compact before-and-after loop. On the left, a slow clock advances while one token rarely leaks outward; the flippase repeatedly returns it inward using ATP tokens. Label this moving balance 'steady state'. On the right, open the scramblase gate and let several tokens cross both ways; the unequal pattern visibly collapses into a mix. No clocks or speed comparison on this side. Keep both membrane diagrams moving.
scenes.narration: Together, slow leakage, pumps, and regulated scrambling create a steady state, not a permanent arrangement. Flippases keep restoring selected lipids. Switching on a scramblase lets the pattern collapse.

scenes.tts: Now predict. Suppose every phospholipid slides sideways, but none crosses to the other leaflet. Will the two faces become mixed?
scenes.visual: Reset to unequal leaflets. All tokens glide rapidly left and right within their own rows, bouncing gently from the frame edges. A large question card appears: 'Sideways only: do the faces mix?' Hold the gold and teal face colours steady.
scenes.narration: Now predict. Suppose every phospholipid slides sideways, but none crosses to the other leaflet. Will the two faces become mixed?

scenes.visual: Thinking pause. Keep the question card and the unequal rows visible. Lipid tokens continue sliding within their rows, never crossing; no new labels appear.

scenes.tts: No. Each leaflet becomes well stirred, yet the lipids remain on their original face. Across and along are independent directions. Lateral diffusion is that motion along the membrane.
scenes.visual: The question card changes to 'No'. Sweep each row into an even spacing while preserving its lipid types. Draw a blocked vertical arrow labelled 'across' and a long moving horizontal arrow labelled 'along'. Enlarge the horizontal arrow as the membrane tokens keep drifting; replace its label with 'lateral diffusion'.
scenes.narration: No. Each leaflet becomes well stirred, yet the lipids remain on their original face. Across and along are independent directions. Lateral diffusion is that motion along the membrane.

scenes.tts: Fluorescence recovery after photobleaching, or F R A P, measures lateral motion. Fluorescent membrane proteins begin bright. A brief laser makes one spot dark. Unbleached proteins then diffuse into it.
scenes.caption: Fluorescence recovery after photobleaching, or FRAP, measures lateral motion. Fluorescent membrane proteins begin bright. A brief laser makes one spot dark. Unbleached proteins then diffuse into it.
scenes.visual: Transform lipid tokens into evenly scattered blue protein blocks with small bright halos, all sliding laterally in the same membrane. A circular viewing window expands to fill the frame. A red laser pulse sweeps across its centre, extinguishing halos inside a round spot while blocks remain present. Bright blocks drift in from both sides and dark blocks drift out; the centre brightens continuously.
scenes.narration: Fluorescence recovery after photobleaching, or FRAP, measures lateral motion. Fluorescent membrane proteins begin bright. A brief laser makes one spot dark. Unbleached proteins then diffuse into it.

scenes.tts: The recovery curve answers two questions. How much fluorescence returns gives the mobile fraction. How quickly it reaches half of that return gives the half-time. Dark molecules still move; bleaching only removed their fluorescence.
scenes.visual: Move the membrane window left and build a computed example curve on the right using F of t equals twenty plus sixty times one minus two to the power negative t over four. Axes read 'time' and 'fluorescence'; plot rises from 20 toward 80. Animate a vertical bracket from 20 to 80 labelled 'recoverable increase', then highlight its halfway level at 50 and time four. Beside the membrane, dark blocks continue moving to make clear they remain present.
scenes.narration: The recovery curve answers two questions. How much fluorescence returns gives the mobile fraction. How quickly it reaches half of that return gives the half-time. Dark molecules still move; bleaching only removed their fluorescence.

scenes.tts: Take the film's computed example. Fluorescence starts at one hundred, falls to twenty, then plateaus at eighty. Sixty units returned, but eighty were bleached. The mobile fraction is sixty divided by eighty, or zero point seven five.
scenes.visual: Enlarge the computed curve and place three moving readout blocks on it: 'before 100', 'after 20', and 'plateau 80'. Transform the vertical rise from 20 to 80 into a bar labelled 'returned 60'. Transform the fall from 100 to 20 into a second bar labelled 'bleached 80'. Slide both into the plain-text calculation '60 divided by 80 = 0.75', then ring 'mobile fraction'.
scenes.narration: Take the film's computed example. Fluorescence starts at one hundred, falls to twenty, then plateaus at eighty. Sixty units returned, but eighty were bleached. The mobile fraction is sixty divided by eighty, or zero point seven five.

scenes.tts: Half of the recoverable increase is thirty. Add that to twenty, making the halfway level fifty. The curve reaches fifty at four seconds, so its recovery half-time is four seconds.
scenes.visual: Return the two bars to the curve. Split the 'returned 60' bar into two equal animated halves of 30. Move one half above the postbleach level 20, landing at the horizontal level 50. A dot travels along the computed curve until it meets 50; a vertical guide drops to '4 seconds'. Replace the guide label with 'half-time'.
scenes.narration: Half of the recoverable increase is thirty. Add that to twenty, making the halfway level fifty. The curve reaches fifty at four seconds, so its recovery half-time is four seconds.

scenes.tts: Under a stated diffusion model, spot size and half-time can estimate a diffusion coefficient. The estimate is approximate because the bleach and membrane must match that model. Binding or barriers can change recovery.
scenes.visual: Keep the computed curve and place a radius ruler across the bleached spot, labelled 'spot size'. Show only one spot size; do not compare spot sizes or half-times. Show labelled blocks 'spot size' and 'half-time' flowing into a box 'diffusion model', which outputs 'approximate D'. Then add a fence across part of the membrane and a tether on one protein; the curve subtly changes and a caution label appears: 'check assumptions'.
scenes.narration: Under a stated diffusion model, spot size and half-time can estimate a diffusion coefficient. The estimate is approximate because the bleach and membrane must match that model. Binding or barriers can change recovery.

scenes.tts: So a membrane can preserve two different faces while its components move. Fast crossing needs a machine; sideways motion does not. Pumps build lipid asymmetry, scramblases erase it, and F R A P measures lateral diffusion.
scenes.caption: So a membrane can preserve two different faces while its components move. Fast crossing needs a machine; sideways motion does not. Pumps build lipid asymmetry, scramblases erase it, and FRAP measures lateral diffusion.
scenes.visual: Return to the large membrane patch. Left third: flippase uses an ATP token to restore unequal lipid rows. Centre: scramblase briefly opens and the rows begin mixing. Right third: a FRAP spot darkens and recovers as protein blocks drift sideways. Then merge the three views into one membrane with a vertical 'fast crossing: machine' arrow and a horizontal 'free diffusion' arrow. Gold cytosol and teal outside remain chapter 1's colours.
scenes.narration: So a membrane can preserve two different faces while its components move. Fast crossing needs a machine; sideways motion does not. Pumps build lipid asymmetry, scramblases erase it, and FRAP measures lateral diffusion.

scenes.visual: End card over the softly moving membrane: 'Fast crossing needs a machine; sliding sideways does not.' Keep a few lipid tokens drifting laterally behind the line.
